svg.title: Submission Tracker architecture
svg.desc: A filter change in the Next.js frontend updates the URL, which is parsed into a canonical query, cached by React Query and sent by the API client to the Django backend. There the view validates the params with a FilterSet, loads rows with a fixed number of SQL queries and serializes them to camelCase JSON, which flows back into the React Query cache and re-renders the screen.

svg.text: Why it is built this way

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The URL is the only store

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: One view = one canonical URL = one cache key, so

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Back, refresh and shared links restore it exactly.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Server data lives in React Query

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Components keep only UI state (open menus, typing).

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Errors map to a fix: Retry, Reset filters, Page 1.

svg.text: A fixed number of SQL queries

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: List 3, detail 4, brokers 1, whatever the page size.

svg.text: Tests count them, so an N+1 regression fails CI.
